- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 85+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when recent history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 75–70 range) — fails to recognize “mean reversion” or “support level” behavior.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts too aggressively downward after minor spikes, missing the “recovery” phase.
- Model tends to underestimate true outcomes when the 30-day history includes a recent low (e.g., 70–72) — fails to recognize “bottoming” or “support” behavior.
- Model often fails to adjust for “seasonal” or “calendar” effects — e.g., forecasts remain high in late November despite historical downward trend.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when the 30-day history includes a recent high (e.g., 80–85) — fails to recognize “overbought” or “peak” behavior.
